title: United Kingdom 1855-1913, annual: union unemployment, real earnings, factor incomes (Mitchell) and the nominal capital stock (Feinstein and Pollard)
source: Bank of England, 'A millennium of macroeconomic data for the UK' (version 3.1): sheet 'A50. Employment & unemployment' (unemployment rate based on unions that offered unemployment benefit schemes to their members, Feinstein (1972)/Board of Trade (adjusted)); sheet 'A48. Real consumption and product wages 1209-2016' (real consumption earnings, GB, index 1900 = 100); sheet 'A17. GDP(I) components' (compensation of employees, Mitchell (1988) Chapter XVI Table 4; gross trading profits and self-employment income, rent, GDP(I) at factor cost, Mitchell (1988) Chapter XVI Table 5; gross trading surplus of other public enterprises); sheet 'A55. Capital Stock Estimates 1760-2016' (nominal value of capital stock, £mn, non-dwellings whole economy and dwellings, UK, Feinstein and Pollard (1988))
series: year; unemp_unions: per cent; real_earnings_1900_100: index, 1900 = 100; employees_gbp_m, profits_selfemp_gbp_m, rent_gbp_m, public_enterprises_gbp_m, gdp_factor_cost_gbp_m: £ million, current prices (the components add up to GDP(I) at factor cost; the surplus of other public enterprises begins in 1889 and is empty before); capital_nondwellings_gbp_m, capital_dwellings_gbp_m: nominal capital stock, £ million
license: The workbook asks users to cite the underlying sources ('When using this data, please cite this source'). The Bank of England publishes it as a research dataset; a subset is stored here for teaching, with attribution to the Bank of England and to the authors of the series.
notes: Workbook SHA-256 4c23dd392a498691eac92659aec283fb43f28118bd80511dc87fc595974195eb (the copy used for boe_millennium_gb_1790_1830 and boe_millennium_gb_1822_1827_monthly). The script checks the headings of each column it reads. Gross trading profits include the income of the self-employed, so the profit share overstates the share of capital; the chapter's ratio of profits to the non-dwelling capital stock is a rough proxy for Marx's rate of profit (it uses a gross income and a capital stock at current prices, and leaves out rent and dwellings), not a measurement of it. The union unemployment rate covers only the unions that paid unemployment benefit to their members, not the whole labour force.
citation: Feinstein, C. H. (1972), National Income, Expenditure and Output of the United Kingdom 1855-1965, Cambridge University Press; Mitchell, B. R. (1988), British Historical Statistics, Cambridge University Press; Feinstein, C. H. and S. Pollard (eds) (1988), Studies in Capital Formation in the United Kingdom 1750-1920, Oxford: Clarendon Press; data via Bank of England, A Millennium of Macroeconomic Data for the UK, v3.1 (R. Thomas and N. Dimsdale, 2017)
